issues.display_title: Issue #651: Handle Issue Support Menu Appears When Accessing the Profile Page
issues.main_description_html:
• The support menu should appear only for the support role

RESULT

Branch: fix/651-support-menu-sidebar · Commit: a52ae17

What was actually wrong

The opposite of the title: Support was not leaking onto Profile, it was missing everywhere else. hasSupportAccess and accountNavItemsFor were already correct and are untouched — the sidebar simply was not always told who is signed in.

Caller What it passed Result for a support user
AccountShell.tsx:58 (Profile, Billing, Help…) email + role from the user store Support shown ✅
app/dashboard/page.tsx:66 nothing — <DashboardSidebar /> accountNavItemsFor({}) filtered it out ❌

Same session, same role, two different menus. The dashboard already had user in scope from useDashboard(); it just never handed it to the sidebar.

Fix

DashboardSidebar reads the shared user record itself (useUserStore), keeping the props as an override for callers that already hold it — one guard inside the component instead of a prop threaded through every caller, so the next page that renders a bare sidebar cannot reintroduce it.

Files: src/components/dashboard/DashboardSidebar.tsx, src/components/dashboard/__tests__/DashboardSidebar.test.tsx (new).

Checks

tsc --noEmit pass · eslint pass · vitest 138 files, 1104 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed — 5 new tests: role from the store with no props, non-support role hidden, signed-out hidden, explicit prop honoured, shared destinations intact. The first was confirmed to fail without the fix, so it is not a vacuous test.

Worth a follow-up

This fix is right regardless of role data, but it was never confirmed that the account in the screenshot actually holds the support role. If it does not, something upstream is granting it — a separate and security-relevant question.

issues.display_title: Issue #652: Handle Issue Description is Short, but there is a “Show More” toggle
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT

Branch: fix/652-show-more-only-when-clamped · Commit: d1b1612

Cause

PreviewInfoCard.tsx:154 rendered the toggle for every description that existed. The paragraph carries line-clamp-3, but nothing ever asked whether the clamp actually bit — so a one-line note like "ruang tester" got a Show More that expands one line into the same one line.

Fix

The card measures it: a ref on the paragraph, scrollHeight > clientHeight while the clamp is on, re-measured through a ResizeObserver because the same text clamps at one card width and not at another. The toggle renders only when the text is genuinely cut off.

Length of the string would not do — three lines is a CSS clamp, and whether the text reaches it depends on the card width and the font, so only the browser knows.

The button also stays while the description is expanded: once unclamped nothing overflows, and dropping it there would strand the reader with no way back.

Files: src/components/editor/preview/PreviewInfoCard.tsx, src/components/editor/preview/__tests__/PreviewInfoCard.test.tsx.

Checks

tsc --noEmit pass · eslint pass · vitest 138 files, 1106 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed.

Two new tests: a description that already fits renders no toggle, and Show Less survives expansion. jsdom lays nothing out (scrollHeight === clientHeight === 0) and has no ResizeObserver, so the tests stub the two heights and the component skips the observer when it is absent — which covers SSR as well. The first new test was confirmed to fail without the fix.

issues.display_title: Issue #672: Editor Map: floor stack snap for Selected Floor placement (PRD #594)
issues.main_description_html:
Stacking a multi-floor building in Editor Map mode is trial and error. Selected Floor placement already writes level.mapTransform.offsetX/offsetY from both drag (src/lib/map/useBuildingDrag.ts:107-117) and the nudge D-pad (src/components/editor/MapTransformControl.tsx:238-246), but nothing helps the creator land a floor on the one below it — a six-floor building can ship one floor visibly off.

PRD #594 asks for a Snap mode on Selected Floor placement: with snap on, moving the active floor aligns it to another floor in the same building once it comes within tolerance, by footprint center or footprint edge. Snap writes offset only — never rotation, never scale.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What already holds (no code needed)

Validated against the code before scoping — six of the PRD's twelve acceptance criteria are already true:

PRD AC Why it already holds
Applies only in Selected Floor scope Snap sits inside the existing scope === "floor" branches; every other scope is a different branch
Writes only the active floor offset patchLevelTransform (src/lib/map/placement.ts:15) takes a patch object that is literally { offsetX, offsetY }
Never changes rotationDeg / scale same patch object
Siblings, building and project transforms do not move covered by src/lib/map/__tests__/placement.test.ts:61-66; the building pivot buildingBBoxCenter (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:182) is computed from untransformed level centers, so a floor offset provably cannot move the building frame
Save/reload preserves alignment mapTransform lives inside canvasData, autosaved at 2 s
Inert in outdoor mode Editor Map has no outdoor mode. useAutoOutdoor has one caller, PreviewOverlay.tsx, which mounts only under previewMode. Editor3DMapView imports useOutdoorLayer — a layer, not a mode. The comment at MapTransformControl.tsx:333-336 claiming otherwise is stale and should be corrected in this task

The snap arithmetic is also far smaller than it looks: makeLevelLocalTransform (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:151) rotates and scales about the level's own bbox center, so a level's placed center is exactly levelBBoxCenter(level) + (offsetX, offsetY) no matter how it is rotated or scaled — pinned today by geojson-level-transform.test.ts:49-56. Candidates in the same building share every frame above them, so the whole calculation is subtraction in local model px. No lng/lat, no frame composition, no new geometry code: levelBBox and levelBBoxCenter already exist and only need exporting.

Scope

  • src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts — export levelBBox (:131) and levelBBoxCenter (:145)
  • src/lib/map/placement.ts — snapFloorOffset(cd, levelId, offsetX, offsetY, tol) returning { offsetX, offsetY, snappedTo }, plus moveLevelByMapStep(...), the shared point drag and nudge both route through. They have no shared commit path today; patchLevelTransform is not one, since it also carries rotation-only and scale-only patches
  • src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts — floorStackSnapEnabled: boolean + setter, following mapMoveMode (:24, :136, :205). Session-only by construction: nothing persists unless hand-copied into buildPersistedState (src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts:50)
  • src/lib/map/useBuildingDrag.ts — route the floor branch through the shared helper. The snap flag goes in a ref alongside the others (:60-72), never in the effect deps (:174) — a remount there commits an in-flight drag
  • src/components/editor/MapTransformControl.tsx — same helper in handleNudge; Snap toggle in the popup beside Reset (:446-453), rendered only when floorScope (:299); fix the stale outdoor comment
  • src/components/editor/Editor3DMapView.tsx — pass the flag/tolerance into useBuildingDrag; append the matched floor to the existing move-mode hint (:356)
  • src/lib/map/__tests__/floorSnap.test.ts (new)

Out of scope: building-to-building snap, cross-building snap, rotation/scale snap, schema changes, preview and live viewer.

Decisions to make while building

  1. Tolerance must stay well under computeBBox span x 0.02. The nudge step is 2% of the whole-model span (MapTransformControl.tsx:233-235) and accumulates from current state, so a tolerance at or above one step traps the floor: every arrow click moves one step and snap pulls it straight back. Drag is immune — it recomputes from the pre-drag snapshot. Alternative if the margin is too tight: nudge snaps only on the click that enters tolerance.
  2. Candidate set. All same-building floors, or only the rendered ones? The editor draws levelsAtOrBelow (src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLayer.ts:193), so snapping floor 2 to floor 5 jumps toward geometry that is not on screen. Restricting candidates to the rendered set is cheaper and self-explaining.

Deliberately trimmed from the PRD

  • No separate floorSnap.ts — placement.ts is already the shared home of every placement write, and is already unit-tested
  • Feedback is the text in the existing move-mode chip, not a MapLibre guide-line layer. Floors below already render as ghost geometry, so a snap is visibly an alignment; a guide line means a new source, a new layer, a style-reload re-add and teardown. Add one later only if beta users say they cannot tell
  • Four unit tests, not the PRD's twelve plus five component tests. "Rotation unchanged" and "scale unchanged" assert an object literal; "siblings do not move" is placement.test.ts:61-66; "drag and nudge behave the same" stops being a behaviour once both call one function. The component tests need the full store plus a fake MapLibre and would pin markup the design branch still churns
  • Edge snapping stays in, but as a Should, not a Must: same-building floors usually share a footprint, where edge and center land on the same point. It must not grow into per-corner or per-wall alignment

Acceptance

  • Snap toggle appears in the map transform popup, only under Selected Floor scope
  • Snap candidates are floors in the selected building; the active floor is excluded; floors with no usable footprint are skipped
  • Drag applies snap within tolerance; nudge applies the same snap and stays escapable
  • Center-to-center and left/right/top/bottom edge alignment both work
  • Snap writes only offsetX/offsetY; rotation and scale unchanged; siblings, building and project frames unchanged
  • With no eligible candidate, drag and nudge behave exactly as today
  • The matched floor is named in the move-mode hint while a snap is applied
  • Save and reload preserve the snapped alignment
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Source PRD: #594 (docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-10-floor-stack-snap-mode/prd.md, branch product-docs).

RESULT

Branch: feature/672-floor-stack-snap-prd (from development) · Commits: 2ed8ab4, 6064f75

PRD #594 implemented as written. Two versions were built and compared; this is the full PRD one. The scoped alternative (443 lines, text-only feedback, no separate helper module, four unit tests) sits on feature/672-floor-stack-snap and was not taken.

Snap

Selected Floor placement gets a Snap toggle. With it on, moving the active floor pulls it onto another floor of the same building once it comes within tolerance — footprint centre to centre, or matching edge to edge (left to left, right to right, top to top, bottom to bottom). Opposite edges are never paired. The two axes snap independently, so a floor can catch one edge while still moving freely along the other.

Candidate filtering, the alignment arithmetic and the guide geometry all live in one pure module, src/lib/map/floorSnap.ts, reached by drag and by the nudge D-pad through the same moveLevelByMapStep. That answers both risks the PRD names in §9: cross-building candidates cannot leak in, and drag and nudge cannot drift apart.

Tolerance, and why the arrows still work

Tolerance is 1% of the active floor's raw footprint span, overridable per call via options.tolerance.

Relative, because a fixed pixel count means nothing without the model's size — one that feels right on a shop is invisible on an airport.

Measured off the raw span because the pull has to stay escapable. The nudge D-pad steps 2% of the whole model's span and accumulates from the current offset, so a tolerance at or above one step would drag the floor back onto the target every click and trap it there. computeBBox spans every level's raw geometry, so one floor's raw span can never exceed the model's — 1% of a floor is always under 2% of the model, whatever that floor's rotation or scale. One arrow always out-steps the pull. Drag is immune anyway: it recomputes from the pre-drag snapshot every move, so the floor lets go the moment the cursor leaves tolerance.

Why the arithmetic is small

makeLevelLocalTransform rotates and scales a level about its own footprint centre, so a level's placed centre is exactly levelBBoxCenter + (offsetX, offsetY) no matter how it is turned — already pinned by geojson-level-transform.test.ts:49-56. Same-building candidates share every frame above them, so no frame composition is needed and the whole calculation is subtraction in building-frame model px.

Only offsetX/offsetY are ever written. Rotation and scale are read, because they change the box a floor presents, and never written. Sibling floors keep object identity, and the building pivot buildingBBoxCenter is computed from untransformed level centres — so a floor offset provably cannot move the building or project frame.

Feedback

A dashed guide on each matched axis, spanning both footprints, plus the matched floor's name in the move-mode hint. The guides are drawn in the building frame — via a new makeBuildingFramePixelTransform — not the active floor's own, which is the thing being aligned: projecting through it would drag the guide along with the floor instead of leaving it on the target. Both cues clear when the match goes, when the gesture ends, when Snap is switched off, and when the floor, building or scope changes.

The transient match lives in the store rather than local state because nudge is raised in MapTransformControl while the guide is drawn from Editor3DMapView. It is never persisted — the persist allowlist in wizardState.ts is hand-written, so anything not copied there is session-only by construction.

Control placement

The toggle sits in the map transform popup, shown in every scope but inert outside Selected Floor rather than hidden. A control that disappears when the scope changes reads as a bug, and the disabled tooltip is where the rule gets taught — PRD §9's first risk is "users may not realize snap applies only to Active Floor scope". With no eligible floor in the building the toggle still works and the tooltip says why, so there is no dead end.

Performance

Snap asks every candidate floor for its bounding box on every mousemove, and finding one tessellates each curved wall. Measured on a six-floor building of 300 bezier walls each: 7.344 ms per mousemove, past the frame budget before MapLibre had drawn anything.

levelBBox now caches on the geometry object. A level is re-created on every placement write while its layout is carried across untouched, so keying there survives a drag and still misses when the geometry is really edited — nothing mutates a layout in place, every writer builds a fresh one. Same move now costs 0.049 ms.

Separately, location was a fresh { lat, lng } literal per render and sits in useFloorPlanLayer's dependency list, so any unrelated re-render of the map view rebuilt and re-pushed the whole model's GeoJSON. Memoized.

R14 — outdoor mode

Satisfied vacuously, with no code. Editor Map mode has no outdoor state: useAutoOutdoor has one caller, PreviewOverlay, which mounts only under previewMode; Editor3DMapView imports useOutdoorLayer, which is a context-shell layer, not a mode. The Overview state was removed from Editor Map by #591 R1-R6. A stale comment in MapTransformControl.tsx claiming these controls guarded against it has been dropped. The PRD's manual-QA item "confirm outdoor mode prevents snap placement edits" is not executable in Editor Map.

Tooling

pnpm test and pnpm lint were failing before this branch, on the scratch worktrees under .claude/ — whole second checkouts of this repo, already ignored by git. Vitest ran every suite twice and failed on the stale copy; eslint died on a file that checkout no longer has. Both now skip .claude/**. No worktree was deleted.

Files

 src/lib/map/floorSnap.ts                                  | 228 +++++  (new)
 src/lib/map/useSnapGuideLayer.ts                          | 114 +++++  (new)
 src/lib/map/__tests__/floorSnap.test.ts                   | 218 +++++  (new)
 src/lib/map/__tests__/snapInteraction.test.tsx            | 207 +++++  (new)
 src/components/editor/__tests__/MapTransformControl.snap.test.tsx | 185 +++++  (new)
 src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts                              |  58 ++--
 src/components/editor/Editor3DMapView.tsx                 |  50 ++--
 src/components/editor/MapTransformControl.tsx             |  66 ++--
 src/lib/map/useBuildingDrag.ts                            |  43 ++--
 src/lib/map/placement.ts                                  |  27 ++
 src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts                         |  17 ++
 vitest.config.ts                                          |   7 +-
 eslint.config.mjs                                         |   4 +

Checks

pnpm test 142 files, 1153 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed · pnpm lint clean · tsc --noEmit clean.

PRD §7's nine unit cases in its own order, plus the guide geometry and the escapability invariant. All five component/interaction cases: the popup control renders for Selected Floor, is inert outside it, the nudge arrows snap, a real drag runs through the hook against a fake maplibre (so the whole lngLat → metres → px → frame chain is exercised, not a re-implementation of the rule), and the guide appears and clears.

issues.display_title: Issue #673: Mappedin import: floors arrive in the export's arbitrary order — sort each floor stack by floors.geojson elevation
issues.main_description_html:
Fixes the report in #628: a Mappedin import lands in the project in an order that is not the order the file describes.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Asset: the reporter's own export — Multi-Family Hi-Rise Demo, 36 floors, one floor stack (.playwright-mcp/demo/628/mappedin-hi-rise-36-floors.zip)

Evidence

.playwright-mcp/demo/628/video-628-floor-order.mp4 — the same file imported twice, development on the left half of the run and the fix on the right, read straight out of the review modal:

BEFORE  Level 1 | Mezzanine | Level 2 | Level 3 | Level 4 | RA | Level 24 | Level 17 | …
        …ending: Level 34 | PH | Level 18 | Level 16     ← badge "1" = the ground floor
AFTER   RA | PH | Level 34 | Level 33 | … | Level 2 | Mezzanine | Level 1

The BEFORE line is byte-for-byte the level dropdown in #628's screenshot. The AFTER line is byte-for-byte the Mappedin reference viewer beside it.

Root cause

src/lib/mappedin/parse.ts:76 and :87:

let floorIds = floorStacks.flatMap((stack) => stack.floors ?? []);
// "Do NOT sort by floors.geojson `elevation`: it's an entry-floor ordinal … not a physical height."
floorIds.reverse();

The parser assumes floor-stacks.json lists floors top-first and reverses it. It does not list them in any physical order at all. In the reporter's file the stack reads Level 1, Mezzanine, Level 2, Level 3, Level 4, RA, Level 24, Level 17, Level 8, Level 19, Level 33, … — neither ascending nor descending — so reversing it produces a reversed scramble, which is exactly what shipped.

reverse() survived #369 because every sample available then was 1–2 floors, where reversing and sorting are indistinguishable (Airport Demo: Level 2 elevation 0, Level 1 elevation −1).

The real order is floors.geojson elevation, which the file carries on 100% of features and which the current FloorsGeoJson type does not even read. Per the MVF v3 spec it is required, an integer ordinal, 0 = ground, negatives below grade, and unique within a floor stack rather than within the file. Mappedin's own Web SDK sorts its level selector by it. The #369 comment's premise ("not a physical height") is true; its conclusion ("not a sort key") is false, and it is self-refuting — −1 < 0 puts Airport's Level 1 below Level 2, which is right.

Fix

Order each stack by its own elevation, ascending, which is the app's canvasData.levels contract (bottom→top, levelBaseHeights).

Per stack, not globally — elevation is only unique inside one stack, so a global sort over the flattened list interleaves buildings and breaks the invariant documented at src/lib/mappedin/types.ts:86. floorIds is now derived from buildings.flatMap(...), so the two orders are structurally incapable of disagreeing, and the per-stack .reverse() disappears with no replacement.

Missing or non-finite elevation falls back to the feature's own position in floors.geojson — not to 0, which would drop an unannotated floor next to the ground floor.

Files: src/lib/mappedin/parse.ts, src/lib/mappedin-import/extractFloors.ts (stale comment), src/lib/mappedin/__tests__/{fixtures,parse.test,sample-zip.int.test}.ts.

Tests

  • unscrambles a real 36-floor stack listed in arbitrary order — fixture built from the reporter's actual file order, verified byte-for-byte against the zip. Fails under reverse() and under any verbatim pass-through.
  • sorts the floors.geojson fallback when floor-stacks.json is missing
  • sorts each stack separately — elevation is unique per stack, not per file — two stacks with colliding 0..2; buildings must stay contiguous.
  • keeps floors.geojson order when the export carries no elevation
  • Fixtures gained elevation so the sort is actually exercised in CI — samples/ is gitignored, so the integration test skips there.

Acceptance

  • A multi-floor Mappedin import reaches the project in the order Mappedin itself shows.
  • Floors of a multi-building export stay contiguous per building; no interleaving.
  • An export with no elevation keeps its file order rather than being reversed.
  • Airport Demo (negative elevation) still imports Level 1 then Level 2.
  • tsc --noEmit, eslint, vitest green.

Manual verification

  1. New project → import mappedin-hi-rise-36-floors.zip.
  2. The review modal reads RA, PH, Level 34 … down to Mezzanine, Level 1.
  3. Continue to Editor → the floor selector shows the same order.
  4. Re-import a single-floor export and an image-only flow — both unchanged.

Out of scope

  • Projects already imported keep their scrambled order. src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts hydrates canvasData.levels verbatim and there is no migration; the reporter must re-import. Worth a release note.
  • Go backend divergence. Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO/src/utils/mappedin.go:348-357 appends stack.Floors verbatim and never reads elevation, so /v1/import/mappedin still returns the scrambled order. Nothing in src/ calls the proxy routes today, so nothing regresses — but the two parsers now disagree. Flagged per CLAUDE.md; needs its own BE task on Project #112.
  • src/lib/mappedin-editor (the .txt editor export) carries no floor or elevation signal at all, so it cannot exhibit this bug.

RESULT

Branch: fix/673-mappedin-floor-order · Commit: 1174be2 · 5 files, +120/−39 · merged into development as 7256f20

What changed

src/lib/mappedin/parse.ts now sorts each floor stack by its own floors.geojson elevation, ascending — the app's bottom→top canvasData.levels contract — instead of reversing the file's order. Both .reverse() calls are gone.

  • Per stack, not globally. MVF v3 scopes elevation uniqueness to the floorStack, so a global sort over the flattened list would interleave buildings. floorIds is now derived from buildings.flatMap((b) => b.floorIds), which makes ParsedFloor order and ParsedBuilding.floorIds structurally unable to disagree — the invariant documented at types.ts:86 is true by construction for the first time, and the per-stack reverse retires with no replacement.
  • Fallback is position, not zero. A missing or non-finite elevation keeps the feature's own index in floors.geojson; ?? 0 would strand an unannotated floor beside the ground floor. Only reachable for pre-v3 exports — elevation is required in v3 and present on 100% of features in all four real assets.
  • The #369 comments in parse.ts and extractFloors.ts were rewritten, not deleted, and cite the spec: the sort was introduced once before (1474ecd), reverted 28 minutes later (591b246), and replaced by reverse() ten minutes after that (2c3084f). The comment is why it stayed broken.

Verification against the reporter's own file

.playwright-mcp/demo/628/video-628-floor-order.mp4 — 1920×1080, 60 fps, 91 s — imports the same export twice, development first and the fix second, reading the review modal both times:

BEFORE  Level 1 | Mezzanine | Level 2 | Level 3 | Level 4 | RA | Level 24 | Level 17 | …
        …ending: Level 34 | PH | Level 18 | Level 16      ← badge "1" = the ground floor
AFTER   RA | PH | Level 34 | Level 33 | … | Level 2 | Mezzanine | Level 1

BEFORE is byte-for-byte the dropdown in #628's screenshot; AFTER is byte-for-byte the Mappedin reference viewer beside it. Frames: check-30.png (RA wedged between Level 4 and Level 24), check-44.png (before, "Level 16" as the ground floor), check-78.png (after, Level 1 at the bottom).

The same chain was run headlessly through parse → runImport → groupFloorsByBuilding → mergeImportIntoProject → buildFloorOptions, and against the pre-fix parse.ts to confirm the reproduction rather than assume it.

Checks

tsc --noEmit pass · eslint pass · vitest 139 files, 1129 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed

Four new tests in parse.test.ts, the decisive one built from the reporter's actual 36-floor file order (verified byte-for-byte against the zip) — it fails under reverse() and under any verbatim pass-through. Fixtures gained elevation, without which every fixture-driven test would have exercised only the fallback and the sort would have shipped with no CI coverage: samples/ is gitignored, so the integration test skips in CI.

Still open

  • Projects imported before this fix keep their scrambled order — persistence/wizardState.ts hydrates verbatim and there is no migration. The reporter must re-import. Release note needed.
  • The Go backend still appends stack.Floors verbatim (mappedin.go:348-357); needs its own task on Project #112.

issues.display_title: Issue #676: Access parent resolution: stamp the origin level on placement, so a lift drawn upstairs is not re-parented to its own copy
issues.main_description_html:
Closes the last gap in the Front End Developer TODO of #666 (PRD: door-based building connectors and Access parent-child controls). Everything else in that list shipped in 4282141; this is the one rule that did not survive contact with the authoring flow.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Design: #671 (closed) — no code on design/door-based-building-connectors; that branch still points at a8305ee, an old development.

The bug

Draw a Lift on Level 3, then set Downstairs = Level 2, Level 1. The moment the children appear, the object you drew stops being the parent:

  • the Level 3 card flips to the child card — "Managed by parent · Type and connected floors are set on Level 1"
  • Level 1 — a copy the editor generated seconds ago — inherits Type, Downstairs and Upstairs
  • View parent on the object the user authored navigates down to its own clone
  • in Map mode the Not linked badge moves to the generated copy, so the Information link is offered on the wrong marker (MapObjectMarkers.tsx:128, SelectedFeaturePanel.tsx)

Only groups that grow downward are visibly wrong. A parent on the ground floor connecting upward already sits first in level order, so the fallback happens to pick it — which is why this reads as correct in the common case and inverts in the multi-storey one the PRD is about.

Root cause

accessParent (src/lib/editor/access.ts:58) resolves in the PRD's documented order — stored origin → earliest createdAt → first member in stored level order.

Rule 1 is dead code for everything the editor creates. accessOriginLevelId is written in exactly one place, migrateLegacyAccess (access.ts:390), which only runs on pre-#585 projects. interactions.ts:181 places a new marker with neither field, and the bridge stamps createdAt only.

Rule 2 cannot break the tie. withAccessSpan clones the template verbatim — const copy = { ...template, id: makeId(), x, y } (access.ts:302) — so every generated child carries the parent's own createdAt. stamped.reduce((a, b) => b.createdAt < a.createdAt ? b : a) never sees a smaller value and keeps its seed.

So every group authored in the editor falls through to rule 3, the legacy last resort: first member in stored level order = the lowest floor.

createdAt is not the place to fix this — it is also the object list's sort key (#392, objectRows.ts:99), and dropping it from copies would sink them to the bottom of their floor's list.

Fix

Stamp accessOriginLevelId where createdAt is already stamped: modelToLevel in src/lib/floorplanEditor/bridge.ts, the single choke point every editor change flows through on its way to the store.

accessPoints: (model.access ?? []).map((ap) => {
  const was = prevAccessById.get(ap.id);
  return {
    ...ap,
    accessOriginLevelId:
      ap.accessOriginLevelId ?? was?.accessOriginLevelId ?? (was ? undefined : prev.level_id),
    createdAt: keep(ap.createdAt ?? was?.createdAt, !prevAccessIds.has(ap.id)),
  };
}),

Only a marker this floor has never seen is stamped. A generated copy already carries the origin it was cloned from (the spread in withAccessSpan preserves it), so it is left alone — re-stamping would make every floor its own origin, which is every member claiming to be the parent. Markers already in prev without an origin are pre-#666 data and stay unstamped, resolving exactly as they do today.

One field, one call site. accessParent, accessDirections, isAccessChild, the two cards and the routing side all read it unchanged.

Tests

src/lib/floorplanEditor/__tests__/bridge.test.ts

  • stamps the origin level onto a marker this floor has never seen — the proof. Reverting the bridge change fails this test and only this test.
  • leaves a generated copy's origin alone on the floor it landed on
  • does not backfill an origin onto markers prev already held

src/lib/editor/__tests__/access.test.ts

  • keeps the drawn marker as parent after it connects floors below — the reported flow end to end: marker on L3, span down to L1/L2, parent stays drawn and accessDirections reads { down: [L2, L1], up: [] }.
  • cannot identify the drawn marker from timestamps alone — pins why the origin carries this and not createdAt: it asserts the copy inherits createdAt: 100 and that accessParent therefore picks the wrong member. Guards the fix against being "simplified" back into rule 2.

Acceptance

  • A Lift drawn on an upper floor stays the parent after Downstairs is set.
  • The parent card keeps Type / Downstairs / Upstairs; the generated copies show the child card.
  • View parent from a child navigates to the floor the marker was drawn on.
  • The Not linked badge appears on the drawn marker, not on a generated copy.
  • Existing projects resolve their parents exactly as before — no backfill, no re-parenting on load.
  • tsc --noEmit, eslint, vitest green.

Manual verification

  1. Multi-floor project → Access tool → place a Lift on Level 3.
  2. Selection card → Down lift → tick Level 2 and Level 1.

RESULT

Branch: fix/676-access-parent-origin · Commit: d914aba · 3 files, +92/−4
Merged: development as 7ed5ce3 (PR #678) → main as c74ed0b (PR #679)

What changed

modelToLevel (src/lib/floorplanEditor/bridge.ts) now stamps accessOriginLevelId onto a marker the floor has never seen, alongside the createdAt stamp that was already there. That is the single choke point every editor change flows through on its way to the store, so it covers placement without touching the create site.

Only a first sighting is stamped. A copy generated by withAccessSpan already carries the origin it was cloned from and is left alone — re-stamping would make every floor its own origin, which is every member claiming to be the parent. Markers already in prev without one are pre-#676 data and stay unstamped, so nothing re-parents on load.

createdAt was deliberately not touched: it is also the object list's sort key (#392, objectRows.ts:99), and dropping it from copies would sink them to the bottom of their floor's list.

Why the first two resolution rules were dead

  • accessOriginLevelId was written in exactly one place, migrateLegacyAccess (access.ts:390), which only runs on pre-#585 projects. interactions.ts:181 placed a new marker without it.
  • withAccessSpan clones the template verbatim (access.ts:302), so every child carried the parent's own createdAt and stamped.reduce(...) never saw a smaller value.

Every group authored in the editor therefore fell to rule 3 — first member in stored level order, the lowest floor.
